turns.content: Let D be both the distance from A to B and the river current's constant speed. If drifting takes 30 minutes, write the trip equation.
Let c be Serge's paddling speed in still water while c also denotes the river current. When he paddles downstream, the trip takes 18 minutes. Write the trip equation.
Use the two observed trip rates to isolate Serge's still-water paddling speed p. Explain why the current rate must be subtracted from the downstream rate.
Evaluate p as a multiple of D per minute.
Use that still-water rate to calculate the time needed to cover distance D with no current.
Report the still-water travel time in minutes and verify it by comparing the three rates.
